key_insight: A deep learning system can analyze full-length ulcerative colitis endoscopy videos to classify disease activity and map inflammation spatially with a continuous disease score.
clinical_relevance: This could make endoscopic assessment more standardized by capturing both overall severity and the distribution of inflammation, including signals linked to histologic healing.
method: Full-length colonoscopy or flexible sigmoidoscopy videos from adults with ulcerative colitis were segmented and annotated using Mayo Endoscopic Score and UCEIS.
A deep learning model performed frame-level quality control and severity prediction across entire videos.
A Continuous Disease Score was derived from UCEIS predictions to quantify inflammatory burden, spatial extent, and histologic correlation.
evidence_signal: In 67 videos from 59 patients, the model showed good remission agreement (MES=0 kappa 0.76; UCEIS≤1 kappa 0.84) and strong histology prediction (AUROC 0.84–0.87).
watch_item: The study is relatively small and retrospective, so broader validation is needed before routine clinical use.
paper_title: Deep learning-based assessment of ulcerative colitis activity from full-length endoscopic videos with spatial characterisation and histological correlation
